title: OpenAI Executive Fidji Simo Steps Down From Full-Time Role, Moves to Advisory Position
image: /images/news/OpenAI Executive Fidji Simo Steps Down From Full-Time Role, Moves to Advisory Position.webp

author.name: Emily Rodriguez
author.bio: Emily covers AI, technology leadership, and industry trends.

content.text: Another major leadership shakeup is coming to OpenAI after one of the company’s top executives, Fidji Simo, announced she’s stepping down from her full-time role and moving to a part-time advisory role. Simo, who was OpenAI’s executive in charge of AGI deployment and applications, made the decision after a long medical leave, saying she needed to focus on her long-term recovery while still supporting the company in an advisory role.

Simo’s departure represents a big change for OpenAI at a critical juncture in its growth. She joins the company after a long career in technology leadership, including serving as CEO of Instacart and leading large consumer product efforts at Meta Platforms. Her experience in scaling consumer products and leading large technology organizations was seen as a plus as OpenAI shifted from research to a broader commercial strategy.
Fidji Simo’s Role in OpenAI’s Expansion Strategy

Simo first joined OpenAI’s board in 2024, then moved to an executive leadership role focused on applications and product execution. Her appointment was part of a move by CEO Sam Altman to shore up the company’s operational structure so he could focus more on research, computing infrastructure and long-term AI development.

During her tenure at the company, Simo helped define how OpenAI approaches product growth, business operations and the broader deployment of standard artificial intelligence (AI) technology. Her departure from day-to-day duties comes as OpenAI continues to battle aggressively in the fast-growing artificial intelligence market.
Health Problems Lead to Change in Leadership

Simo's decision to step away from full-time work was related to ongoing health issues. Reports said she had apparently taken a medical leave several months earlier due to complications related to a chronic neuroimmune condition. She understood that her recuperation would take more time and focus than she had anticipated, leading her to decide to take on an advisory role instead of managing the day-to-day operations.

The executive has spoken publicly before about managing a chronic condition while shouldering demanding leadership responsibilities. Her decision underscores the difficulties that executives in the upper echelons of the tech world face, with companies often racing at an unprecedented pace and demanding intense engagement from senior leaders.

OpenAI has not characterized Simo’s departure as a strategic disagreement or a performance-related move. The company said, however, that it has recognized her contributions and has expressed its support for her continued service as an adviser. CEO Sam Altman praised Simo’s leadership and the significance of her contributions at a time of rapid growth and change for OpenAI.

Simo will not be involved in day-to-day operations, but her ongoing advisory role ensures that she continues to provide her expertise in product strategy, business growth and organizational leadership to benefit OpenAI. The deal also gives the company continuity in a time of internal restructuring.
OpenAI Reorganizes Roles as Part of Broader Growth Plans

As Simo steps back from full-time leadership, OpenAI is spreading many of her responsibilities across other senior executives. Sources say President Greg Brockman is taking on more ownership of product management, with executives like CFO Sarah Friar, Chief Strategy Officer Jason Kwon, and other business leaders expected to head up different operational areas.

The leadership change is coming at a crucial time for OpenAI, which is looking to expand beyond ChatGPT and build out a broader ecosystem of AI-powered products and services. It is pouring resources into research on artificial general intelligence, AI agents, enterprise applications and the infrastructure to power future artificial intelligence systems.
AI Industry Watches OpenAI’s Next Leadership Phase

Simo’s departure from day-to-day operations also follows a series of leadership changes at the company, known as OpenAI. The company has seen a series of executive leadership changes as it struggles to balance rapid innovation with the challenges of managing a global technology organization.

Industry analysts are watching closely how the company’s leadership structure evolves amid growing competition from rivals including Anthropic, Google DeepMind and other big AI developers. Investors, employees and the wider tech industry will be watching closely to see whether OpenAI is able to balance its ambitious AI goals with operational stability.

Though she has taken a step back from her executive role, Simo is expected to continue to influence the direction of OpenAI through her advisory role. Her departure is a personal change but also another important chapter in the company's swift transformation from an AI research organization into one of the world's most influential technology companies.
